t: #3323 Minimize Connected Groups by Inserting Interval
o: First merge the given intervals into connected groups; between consecutive groups there are gaps. Adding one interval of length ≤ k can bridge a contiguous run of gaps whose total length is ≤ k, fusing that run's groups into one. The answer is (number of groups) − (largest number of gaps coverable). In example 1, gaps are 2 and 2 with k = 3, so we can bridge only one gap: 3 − 1 = 2 groups.
k: Only gaps matter — merge intervals first and work with the gap lengths between groups.
A new interval bridges a contiguous window of gaps with total length ≤ k, so the problem reduces to the longest sliding window with sum ≤ k.
Since exactly one interval must be added, bridging zero gaps (answer = group count) is always achievable.

a.n: Approach 1: Merge + Sliding Window over Gaps
a.i: Merge intervals in O(n log n), extract gap lengths, then slide a window maintaining the sum ≤ k; the widest such window is the number of groups we can fuse.
s: Sort intervals and merge overlapping/touching ones into a list of disjoint groups.
Compute gaps[i] = start of group i+1 − end of group i.
Two pointers: expand right, shrink left while gap sum > k; track the maximum window size.
Return groupCount − maxWindow (0 if no gaps).
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting dominates; merging and the two-pointer sweep are linear.
a.sp: O(n) — merged interval list and gap array.

a.i: Same reduction, but for each right gap index binary-search the smallest left index whose prefix-gap sum stays ≤ k. Slightly more code but handy when gaps arrive in a stream or you prefer deterministic per-index queries.
s: Build prefix sums P over gap lengths.
For each r, binary search the largest l with P[r+1] − P[l] ≤ k.
Track the maximum window; return groupCount − maxWindow.
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting plus m binary searches over the prefix array.
a.sp: O(n) — merged list and prefix sums.

w: Present the sliding window as the primary solution — it is simpler and asymptotically equal. Watch for: touching intervals ([1,2],[2,5]) belonging to one group; gap sums overflowing 32 bits (coordinates up to 10^9); and remembering the new interval may sit entirely inside a group (bridging nothing). Follow-up: add up to j intervals, or maximize the number of groups fused instead.
